audit.recode_to: rule '01 001 0001 00001 000001' (final primary, no secondary marks), kind fixed-dominant unchanged (Henderson's light-non-root exception sáqa/katéla, Baird fn.1 'minute number' of penult cases justify dominant-not-strict); and strike the kich1262 'variant fence' text claiming 'OKMA dialect surveys of K'iche' report final primary + alternating secondaries' -- the secondaries trace to Wikipedia, not OKMA. Since kich1266 is a retired code already aliased to kich1262 and rests on the identical Henderson quotation as kich1262/1263/1264/1265/1267, folding the row into kich1262 outright is the cleaner alternative.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: confirmed verbatim at Henderson 2012 preprint p. 26 (82) in the copy fetched sources now (record had no held file). (2) Source: a 2012 NLLT phonology article with first-hand data partly from the West-Central area (Santa Lucía Utatlán ~ Nahualá); for primary stress it is a good source and agrees with Larsen 1988:21/fn.11 (held), Bennett 2016:495 and Baird 2015:165 (both fetched sources): stress is word-final, with a small class of root-stressed exceptions before light non-root material. (3) The problem is the rule string. '01 101 0101 10101 010101' marks alternating secondary stresses leftward from the ultima. Worldscan receipts (batch_310, tb_128, v_078) show this pattern was generated from Wikipedia's sentence 'on every other syllable before the final in an iambic pattern' (graded tertiary, 'carried-secondary'), which cites Larsen 1988:12-13; those Larsen pages are phoneme tables and Larsen
audit.second_reader_evidence: Independent re-check of every claim in the prior assessment; all confirmed. (1) QUOTE: (45-pp preprint, extracted text) p. 26, sec. 4.1, ex. (82) reads verbatim 'K'ICHEE' STRESS GENERALIZATION Stress falls on the final syllable of a prosodic word, unless that syllable is light non-root material, in which case it falls on the final root syllable.' followed by 'The first part of the generalization is that stress is attracted to the right edge of the prosodic word.' The sentence before (82) says it 'captures the distribution of primary stress in K'ichee''. p. 27: 'K'ichee' cannot be trochaic.

sources.quote: p.21: 'Stress in Quiché always falls on the final syllable'; fn.11: 'Stress in Quiché is regularly placed on the last syllable of a word in isolation' (exception: attributive -V suffix never stressed; 'stress the final syllable of a word which ends in a consonant or in a long vowel'). pp.12-13 are the phoneme/orthography tables; grep of the full text for iamb/secondary stress/every other/alternat returns nothing -- the Wikipedia 'iambic pattern' sentence that generated this record's secondaries is not supported by its own cited source.
